Chapter 7: The Land Remembers — Returning to Africa and the Pull of Home
You know that feeling when you go back to a place that shaped who you are? There’s this mix of nostalgia, a deep longing, and a quiet ache that reminds you everything’s changed—whether you want it to or not. For someone whose first memories are tied to Africa’s red earth and endless skies, coming home after years away feels like both a warm embrace and a moment of truth.
At first glance, it’s almost like nothing’s changed. The acacia trees still stretch their shadows across the ground at dusk, and you can still catch that earthy scent of rain and dust hanging in the air. But if you look closer, you notice that everything’s different beneath the surface. Old friends have moved on, daily routines don’t quite sync up the way they used to, and even familiar places can feel both welcoming and a little strange.
Wandering through those fields, the pilot can’t help but drift back to childhood—remembering what it was like to feel the grass under bare feet, to wake up to the sounds of horses in the morning, and to listen to stories around the fire at night. These memories come with a bittersweet edge, knowing the past can’t be relived. Still, there’s something comforting in how the land keeps going. The earth doesn’t care about our worries; it just endures.
Picture this: standing at the edge of a river, watching a herd of elephants move quietly through the trees. Suddenly, all those old memories come rushing back—days spent tracking animals, or lying awake at night, listening to the distant roar of lions. It hits you that no matter how far you travel, the places that shaped you never really let go.
But let’s be honest—coming home isn’t always easy. The world’s moved on, and so have you. The things you used to count on may not fit the same way anymore, and the future can feel more uncertain than ever. There are moments filled with doubt—questions about where you belong, what your purpose is, and what it truly means to call a place home.
Most people, faced with all that uncertainty, try to hold on to the past or chase after what’s been lost. But the pilot discovered something different: embracing change is part of the journey. The land, with its unending cycles of growth and decay, has its own quiet lesson about resilience. Life keeps moving forward—and, in the end, so should we.
